title: Grade 6 French — Wed, Jun 18
description: La nourriture — Day 3 of 5: Preferences with J'aime / Je n'aime pas
subject: french

questions.question: How do you say 'I love chocolate' in French?
questions.explanation: J'adore means 'I love' (stronger than j'aime = I like). J'adore le chocolat = I love chocolate.

questions.question: Which sentence means 'I don't like fish'?
questions.explanation: Je n'aime pas means 'I don't like'. Je n'aime pas le poisson = I don't like fish.

questions.question: After 'j'aime', 'j'adore', 'je déteste', which article is used with food nouns?
questions.explanation: With verbs of preference (aimer, adorer, détester, préférer), use the definite article (le/la/les). Example: J'aime le riz, Je déteste les épinards.

questions.question: How do you say 'I hate spinach' in French?
questions.explanation: Je déteste means 'I hate'. Les épinards = spinach (plural). Je déteste les épinards = I hate spinach.

questions.question: Which word is the STRONGEST positive preference?
questions.explanation: The scale from weak to strong: Je n'aime pas → J'aime bien → J'aime → J'adore. J'adore expresses the strongest liking.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: '___ les pâtes.' (I like pasta.)
questions.explanation: J'aime les pâtes = I like pasta. J'aime is the correct verb for 'I like'.

questions.question: How do you say 'I prefer vegetables to meat'?
options: Je préfère les légumes à la viande.
Je mange les légumes avant la viande.
Je déteste la viande avec les légumes.
questions.explanation: Je préfère X à Y means 'I prefer X to Y'. Je préfère les légumes à la viande = I prefer vegetables to meat.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct? (I like apples.)
questions.explanation: With preference verbs, use the definite article. Les pommes (apples) = plural definite. J'aime les pommes = I like apples.

questions.question: What does 'je n'aime pas du tout' mean?
questions.explanation: Du tout means 'at all'. Je n'aime pas du tout = I don't like at all. It is a strong negative.

questions.question: How would you ask a friend 'Do you like fruit?' in French?
questions.explanation: Tu aimes les fruits? = Do you like fruit? Aimer + definite article is used for preferences.

questions.question: Which sentence means 'She loves pizza'?
questions.explanation: Elle adore la pizza = She loves pizza. Adorer expresses strong love/liking.

questions.question: How do you say 'I like neither meat nor fish'?
options: Je n'aime pas la viande et le poisson.
Je n'aime ni la viande ni le poisson.
Je déteste la viande et le poisson.
Je ne veux pas la viande ni le poisson.
questions.explanation: Ni… ni… means 'neither… nor…'. Je n'aime ni la viande ni le poisson = I like neither meat nor fish.

questions.question: What does 'j'aime bien' mean compared to 'j'aime'?
options: It means the same as j'aime
questions.explanation: J'aime bien means 'I quite like / I like well enough'. It is a softer, slightly weaker form of j'aime.

questions.question: Which correctly says 'We like vegetables'?
questions.explanation: Nous aimons les légumes = We like vegetables. Use the definite plural article 'les' with preference verbs.

questions.question: Translate: 'They hate carrots.'
questions.explanation: Détester = to hate. Ils détestent les carottes = They hate carrots. Les carottes uses the definite article after détester.
